title: Bounded producer/consumer pipeline
prompt:
Implement `process_all(items, transform, workers=3)`:

- feed `items` through a `queue.Queue` into `workers` daemon threads
- each worker applies `transform(item)` and collects results thread-safely
- `process_all` must RETURN (not hang) once every item is processed, returning `sorted(results)`
- a worker that forgets `task_done()` deadlocks the join — make sure you call it exactly once per item, even when transform raises is NOT required here (transform is assumed safe)
boilerplate:
import threading
import queue

# TODO: process_all(items, transform, workers=3)

tests.name: processes everything and returns
tests.code:
out = process_all([5, 3, 8, 1, 9], lambda x: x * 2, workers=3)
assert out == [2, 6, 10, 16, 18], f'out: {out}'
print('ok')
tests.hint: q.join() releases when unfinished-task count hits zero — exactly one task_done per get().

tests.name: many items, few workers
tests.code:
items = list(range(200))
out = process_all(items, lambda x: x + 1, workers=2)
assert out == [x + 1 for x in range(200)]
print('ok')
tests.hint: All 200 items must be processed by 2 workers; sort for order-independent comparison.
